source.title: Early Warning Signals For Capabilities During Training

record.tranche_reason: The post reports applying a different measure, the 2RDM spectral heat capacity, to detect a known transition in a grokking setting. It does not reproduce the original accuracy and training-set-size measurements.
record.gate_note: The post says the method worked reliably in grokking, but gives no numerical result or grokking-specific breakdown. It also names deep linear networks, induction head formation, and emergent misalignment; those settings are not separate rows because they do not bear on the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The post uses grokking as a known, replicated phase transition to validate its own early-warning method, the 2RDM spectral heat capacity. It reports only that the method 'worked reliably', with no accuracy curves, delay, dataset-size dependence or circuit analysis. That is its own method's performance, not a test of any version. A loss-covariance precursor signal is also a different construct from the gradual circuit formation that V2 names.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The author says the 2RDM behaved 'basically exactly as predicted'. It gave early detection with essentially no tuning on known transitions: deep linear networks, grokking, induction heads and emergent misalignment. The author cautions that probe-set selection matters and becomes harder at scale. The post defers all experimental detail to the preprint.
record.recipe_differences: Uses covariance-based 2RDM and spectral heat capacity to detect transitions; it does not measure the original claim's train/test accuracy trajectory or dataset-size dependence.
record.method_sensitivity: Probe-set selection affects whether the behavior of interest can be detected; the post says this becomes more important as models scale.

fits_no_version.finding: The author states that the 2RDM spectral heat capacity, a variance of eigenvalues of per-sample loss covariance, spiked before the known grokking transition. It did so without tuning. No numbers are given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Correlated per-sample loss fluctuations, measured as spectral heat capacity, provide an early-warning signal that precedes the grokking transition.

record.problems: The post gives only a qualitative summary of the grokking result and defers the full experimental report to the preprint. It supplies no grokking-specific numbers, model or dataset details, uncertainty estimates, or controls.
record.rows_left_out: No additional grokking-specific results are broken out in the post. Results for other named settings were not recorded because they do not bear on the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Train and test accuracy trajectories, the delay after overfitting, and how the delay depends on training-set size.
Gradual formation of a generalizing circuit, later removal of memorizing components, and mechanistic progress measures.
Non-algorithmic data and manipulation of initialization scale or weight norm.
Delayed generalization in LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data.
Weight decay or efficiency account, critical dataset size, and ungrokking.
Comparison of the algorithms learned across runs.
Controls for optimizer or numerical artifacts.

record.verdict_notes: This post summarizes arXiv:2603.29805. Any grokking-specific numbers, such as SHC lead time, model or dataset, would be in the preprint and should be read there before reconsidering a link to V2. Even then, the study evaluates a detection method and would most likely remain T4. The record's 'tests/T2' and its V2 'supports' label are not justified by this text.

versions.untested_parts: Training and test accuracy over time, the delay after overfitting, and how delay changes with training-set size are not reported.

The post reports an early-warning measure for a grokking transition, but does not measure gradual formation of a generalizing circuit, removal of memorizing components, or the mechanism's relation to a test-accuracy jump.
No non-algorithmic-data grokking-like delay or initialization-scale/weight-norm manipulation is reported.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is tested for delayed generalization.
No efficiency account, critical dataset size, or ungrokking result is tested.
The post does not compare algorithms learned across runs.
No optimizer or numerical-artifact controls are reported.

rows.subject: not stated
rows.operation_detail: Use the 2RDM spectral heat capacity as an early-warning signal for a grokking phase transition.
rows.measure: Relative timing of the spectral heat capacity spike and the known phase-transition location
rows.value: The post says the 2RDM worked reliably as an early-detection method in the tested settings, including grokking; it gives no grokking-specific timing or number.
rows.locator: Experimental Results, Probe Selection, and Scaling
rows.note: The post reports the aggregate qualitative result, not a separate grokking measurement or a quantitative lead time.
rows.check: The row reports the study's own method performance on a grokking benchmark, a qualitative statement that the SHC spiked before the known transition. It does not measure circuit formation, memorization removal or the test-accuracy jump. No subject, numbers or lead time are given, so the value cannot be read against V2. It belongs under fits_no_version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
